note: Closed variety of the light ticket form (FR-13): which Jira fields a role sees, what is noise, where an acceptance-criteria section is looked for. Read by scripts/ticket_light.py. A project adds its own custom-field ids in config (direct_api.custom_fields, direct_api.acceptance_criteria_fields); this table never names a project's custom field. The raw response is kept whole elsewhere, so a name missing here hides nothing from the record.
noise_scope_note: A name with no entry here is dropped from every nested object. `id` is dropped from nested objects only (a comment, an attachment and the issue itself keep their own id, spelled out in the projection). `key` is dropped from user objects only (an object that carries displayName, accountId or emailAddress); an issue key stays.
acceptance_headings_note: Matched case-insensitively against a whole line, after an optional h1.-h6. prefix, bold markers and a trailing colon. Config may add more (direct_api.acceptance_headings).
section_names_note: A plain line equal to one of these (case-insensitive, trailing colon allowed) ends an acceptance-criteria section. The other end is the first line that is not a list item and not indented after a blank line. Config may add more.
not_tracker_prefixes_note: Text that has the shape of a tracker key and is not one (UTF-8, ISO-8601, LICENSE-2). Moved here from source_inventory.py NOT_TRACKER_PREFIXES. Project-local plan ids (BE-1, FE-2) cannot be listed: the per-prefix probe settles those. Key shape is uppercase only (tp1-123 is not a key), with no letter or digit glued on either side (fooTP1-9 and TP1-9a are not keys; MY_PROJ-12 is one whole key).

attachment_policy.note_empty_mime: Jira sends a null media type for a file it could not label (a plan.md, a screenshot). Such a file is judged as `empty_mime_as`: never_suffixes is still checked FIRST, so a null-typed .exe, .sh or .zip is never downloaded, and one with an unknown suffix (.bin) is downloaded under the octet-stream limit. A project policy with no `empty_mime_as` key leaves a null type as `type`. blob_suffixes: a stored blob takes the suffix when the media type starts with the prefix or the file name ends with it, so the Read tool opens a PDF as a document; the hash stays over the content; older blobs keep their bare names and are read through local_ref.
attachment_policy.note_text_like: Text-like attachments are ALLOWED under the size limit (a HAR, a log, a JSON or a YAML a person attached is often the evidence a story stands on, and it costs no model tokens to fetch): text/*, application/json and the other text-like media types below, and application/octet-stream, which is where Jira usually files a .yml .yaml .log .har .txt .md .csv. Octet-stream is decided by the file's suffix: the never_suffixes list is checked FIRST, whatever the media type says, so an .exe, .dll, .msi, .sh, .bat, .ps1, an archive or a video is never downloaded even when it is labelled octet-stream; one whose suffix is not on that list is downloaded under the same limit as a document. The code reads only never_suffixes by suffix, so an octet-stream file with an unknown suffix (.bin) is downloaded too, and a text-like file Jira gave a media type no rule names is skipped as `type`. Only executables, archives and video are never downloaded.
